text: Gynecomastia: Gynecomastia is the non-cancerous enlargement of one or both breasts in men due to the growth of breast tissue as a result of a hormone imbalance between estrogens and androgens. Physically speaking, gynecomastia is completely benign, but it is associated with significant psychological distress, social stigma, and dysphoria.

Hypercalcemia: Hypercalcaemia, also spelt hypercalcemia (US), is a high calcium (Ca2+) level in the blood serum. The normal range for total calcium is 2.1–2.6 mmol/L (8.8–10.7 mg/dL, 4.3–5.2 mEq/L), with levels greater than 2.6 mmol/L defined as hypercalcaemia.

Hyperglycemia: Hyperglycemia is an unusually high amount of glucose in the blood. It is defined as blood glucose level exceeding 6.9 mmol/L after fasting for 8 hours or 10 mmol/L (180 mg/dL) 2 hours after eating.

Hypocalcemia: Hypocalcemia (US) or hypocalcaemia (UK) is a medical condition characterized by low calcium levels in the blood serum. The normal range of blood calcium is typically between 2.1 and 2.6 mmol/L, while levels less than 2.1 mmol/L are defined as hypocalcemic.

Hypoglycemia: Hypoglycemia, also spelled hypoglycaemia or hypoglycæmia, sometimes called low blood sugar, is a fall in blood sugar to levels below normal, typically below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L). Whipple's triad is used to properly identify hypoglycemic episodes.

Hypothyroidism: Hypothyroidism is an endocrine disease in which the thyroid gland does not produce enough thyroid hormones. It can cause a number of symptoms, such as poor ability to tolerate cold, extreme fatigue, muscle aches, constipation, slow heart rate, depression, and weight gain.
Thyroid swelling: A presenting complaint characterised by thyroid swelling.

Thyrotoxicosis: Hyperthyroidism is a endocrine disease in which the thyroid gland produces excessive amounts of thyroid hormones. Thyrotoxicosis is a condition that occurs due to elevated levels of thyroid hormones of any cause and therefore includes hyperthyroidism.

Autosomal dominant hypocalcemia: A genetic disorder characterized by low serum calcium, high serum phosphate, and low urinary calcium excretion due to activating mutations in the calcium-sensing receptor or GNA11 gene. Common presenting complaints: Hypocalcemia. Associated symptoms: none listed. Risk factors: none listed. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Autosomal dominant hypocalcemia red flags. Red flag (RF_HYPOCALCEMIC_CRISIS) triggered by complaint 'HYPOCALCEMIA': [LLM DRAFT] Severe symptomatic hypocalcemia presenting with carpopedal spasm, tetany, laryngospasm, or generalized seizures requiring immediate intravenous calcium administration..

Autosomal dominant hypocalcemia differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Cows Milk Hypocalcemia In Newborn: [LLM DRAFT] Presents in neonates secondary to high phosphate load from cow's milk formula rather than an inherited genetic defect in the calcium-sensing receptor. Compared to Other Neonatal Hypocalcemia: [LLM DRAFT] Encompasses transient causes of low calcium in newborns, such as prematurity or maternal diabetes, distinguished by lack of a lifelong autosomal dominant family history.

Chronic thyroiditis with transient thyrotoxicosis: Chronic thyroiditis with transient thyrotoxicosis is an autoimmune thyroid inflammation that temporarily elevates thyroid hormone levels before returning to euthyroid state. Common presenting complaints: Thyrotoxicosis. Associated symptoms: Weight Gain, Feeling Tired, Constipation, Joint And Muscle Pain, Cold Intolerance, Dry Skin, Hair Loss, Slowed Heart Rate. Risk factors: Genetic And Environmental Factors. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Chronic thyroiditis with transient thyrotoxicosis red flags. Red flag (RF_THYROTOXICOSIS) triggered by complaint 'THYROTOXICOSIS': [LLM DRAFT] Acute thyrotoxic crisis (thyroid storm) characterized by severe hyperpyrexia, tachycardia out of proportion to fever, altered mental status, and gastrointestinal dysfunction..

Chronic thyroiditis with transient thyrotoxicosis differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Thyrotoxicosis With Diffuse Goiter Without Thyrotoxic Crisis Or Storm: [LLM DRAFT] Presence of TSH receptor stimulating antibodies and ophthalmopathy pointing to Graves' disease rather than destructive thyroiditis. Compared to Thyrotoxicosis Factitia Without Thyrotoxic Crisis Or Storm: [LLM DRAFT] Undetectable thyroglobulin levels and low radioactive iodine uptake due to exogenous hormone ingestion. Compared to Other Thyrotoxicosis Without Thyrotoxic Crisis Or Storm: [LLM DRAFT] Markedly elevated ESR and anterior neck pain characteristic of subacute granulomatous thyroiditis.

Congenital hypothyroidism with diffuse goiter: Congenital hypothyroidism (CH) is a thyroid hormone deficiency present at birth. If untreated soon after birth, severe congenital hypothyroidism can lead to growth failure and permanent intellectual disability. Common presenting complaints: Thyroid Swelling, Hypothyroidism. Associated symptoms: none listed. Risk factors: none listed. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Congenital hypothyroidism with diffuse goiter red flags. Red flag (RF_THYROID_SWELLING) triggered by complaint 'THYROID_SWELLING': [LLM DRAFT] Severe diffuse goiter in a neonate or infant causing acute upper airway obstruction, stridor, or respiratory distress.. Red flag (RF_HYPOTHYROIDISM) triggered by complaint 'HYPOTHYROIDISM': [LLM DRAFT] Severe congenital hypothyroidism presenting with myxedema coma, profound hypothermia, bradycardia, or circulatory collapse..

Congenital hypothyroidism with diffuse goiter differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Congenital Hypothyroidism Without Goiter: [LLM DRAFT] Absent thyroid enlargement on physical examination, typically due to thyroid dysgenesis (agenesis, hypoplasia, or ectopic location). Compared to Dyshormogenetic Goiter: [LLM DRAFT] Caused by an intrinsic enzymatic defect in thyroid hormone synthesis rather than structural absence or iodine deficiency, often presenting with a familial inheritance pattern. Compared to Neonatal Goiter Not Elsewhere Classified: [LLM DRAFT] Diffuse thyroid enlargement present at birth that may be euthyroid or transient, often linked to maternal exposure to antithyroid medications or goitrogens rather than a permanent congenital defect.

Congenital hypothyroidism without goiter: Congenital hypothyroidism (CH) is a thyroid hormone deficiency present at birth. If untreated soon after birth, severe congenital hypothyroidism can lead to growth failure and permanent intellectual disability. Common presenting complaints: Thyroid Swelling, Hypothyroidism. Associated symptoms: none listed. Risk factors: none listed. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Congenital hypothyroidism without goiter red flags. Red flag (RF_HYPOTHYROIDISM) triggered by complaint 'HYPOTHYROIDISM': [LLM DRAFT] Severe myxedema coma characterized by profound lethargy, hypothermia, hypoventilation, and bradycardia in an untreated infant..

Congenital hypothyroidism without goiter differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Congenital Hypothyroidism With Diffuse Goiter: [LLM DRAFT] Presence of thyroid enlargement (goiter) on physical examination rather than an absent or normal-sized gland. Compared to Dyshormogenetic Goiter: [LLM DRAFT] Associated with an enzymatic defect in thyroid hormone synthesis presenting with goiter rather than thyroid dysgenesis or athyreosis. Compared to Hypothyroidism Unspecified: [LLM DRAFT] Broad classification lacking the specific congenital onset and absence of goiter characteristic of the primary neonatal diagnosis.

Cow's milk hypocalcemia in newborn: A neonatal condition characterized by low serum calcium due to inadequate intake or absorption, often associated with cow's milk-based formula feeding. Common presenting complaints: Hypocalcemia. Associated symptoms: none listed. Risk factors: none listed. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Cow's milk hypocalcemia in newborn red flags. Red flag (RF_HYPOCALCEMIA) triggered by complaint 'HYPOCALCEMIA': [LLM DRAFT] Newborn with severe symptomatic hypocalcemia presenting with acute tetany, laryngospasm, or generalized tonic-clonic seizures..

Cow's milk hypocalcemia in newborn differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Other Neonatal Hypocalcemia: [LLM DRAFT] Presents with neonatal hypocalcemia due to causes other than cow's milk formula ingestion, such as prematurity, maternal diabetes, or birth asphyxia. Compared to Autosomal Dominant Hypocalcemia: [LLM DRAFT] Caused by an activating mutation in the calcium-sensing receptor gene (CASR) rather than dietary phosphate overload from cow's milk, often associated with autosomal dominant inheritance and hypocalciuria. Compared to Congenital Hypothyroidism Without Goiter: [LLM DRAFT] Presents with features of thyroid hormone deficiency (e.g., prolonged jaundice, hypotonia, umbilical hernia) rather than the neuromuscular irritability or tetany characteristic of hypocalcemia.

Diabetes mellitus due to underlying condition with hyperglycemia: Diabetes mellitus, commonly known as diabetes, is a group of common endocrine diseases characterized by sustained high blood sugar levels. Diabetes tends to progress in severity, and is due to either a reduced production of the hormone insulin by the pancreas or unresponsiveness of bodily cells to insulin's effects. Common presenting complaints: Hyperglycemia. Associated symptoms: Frequent Urination, Increased Thirst, Increased Hunger. Risk factors: Maternal Smoking. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Diabetes mellitus due to underlying condition with hyperglycemia red flags. Red flag (RF_HYPERGLYCEMIA_CRISIS) triggered by complaint 'HYPERGLYCEMIA': [LLM DRAFT] Severe hyperglycemia accompanied by altered mental status, lethargy, or signs of diabetic ketoacidosis or hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state (e.g., Kussmaul breathing, fruity breath, severe dehydration).. Red flag (RF_HYPOGLYCEMIA_CRISIS) triggered by complaint 'HYPOGLYCEMIA': [LLM DRAFT] Severe hypoglycemia resulting in loss of consciousness, seizures, or inability to safely consume oral carbohydrates requiring parenteral intervention..

Diabetes mellitus due to underlying condition with hyperglycemia differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus With Hyperglycemia: [LLM DRAFT] Absolute insulin deficiency typically presenting with acute ketoacidosis and autoimmune markers. Compared to Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus With Hyperglycemia: [LLM DRAFT] Insulin resistance associated with metabolic syndrome, obesity, and gradual onset without a primary secondary endocrinopathy or exogenous trigger. Compared to Drug Or Chemical Induced Diabetes Mellitus With Hyperglycemia: [LLM DRAFT] Direct temporal association with the initiation of a culprit medication such as glucocorticoids or antipsychotics.

Drug-induced hypoglycemia without coma: Drug-induced hypoglycemia without coma is a sudden drop in blood glucose levels caused by medication, presenting with neuroglycopenic symptoms but no loss of consciousness. Common presenting complaints: Hypoglycemia. Associated symptoms: Headache, Blurred Vision, Shakiness, Dizziness, Weakness, Fatigue, Sweating, Clamminess, Fast Heart Rate, Anxiety, Hunger, Nausea. Risk factors: Medications (insulin, Glinides, And Sulfonylureas), Sepsis, Kidney Failure, Certain Tumors, Liver Disease. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Drug-induced hypoglycemia without coma red flags. Red flag (RF_SEVERE_HYPOGLYCEMIA_PROGRESSION) triggered by complaint 'HYPOGLYCEMIA': [LLM DRAFT] When low blood glucose symptoms rapidly worsen, fail to resolve with oral carbohydrates, or lead to altered mental status, confusion, or focal neurological deficits..

Drug-induced hypoglycemia without coma differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Hypoglycemia Level 1: [LLM DRAFT] Blood glucose is between 54 and 69 mg/dL, often managed independently without requiring severe symptom classification. Compared to Hypoglycemia Level 2: [LLM DRAFT] Blood glucose is below 54 mg/dL, representing a more pronounced hypoglycemic threshold requiring prompt action. Compared to Hypoglycemia Unspecified: [LLM DRAFT] The clinical documentation lacks precise severity grading or explicit etiology regarding the low blood glucose event.

Drug or chemical induced diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia: Sudden onset of hyperglycemia due to exposure to certain drugs or chemicals that impair insulin secretion or action. Common presenting complaints: Hyperglycemia. Associated symptoms: Frequent Urination, Increased Thirst, Weight Loss. Risk factors: Body Does Not Produce Enough Insulin. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Drug or chemical induced diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia red flags. Red flag (RF_HYPERGLYCEMIA) triggered by complaint 'HYPERGLYCEMIA': [LLM DRAFT] Severe drug-induced hyperglycemia presenting with acute confusion, lethargy, or signs of diabetic ketoacidosis such as Kussmaul breathing and fruity breath odor.. Red flag (RF_HYPOGLYCEMIA) triggered by complaint 'HYPOGLYCEMIA': [LLM DRAFT] Severe drug-induced hypoglycemia presenting with altered mental status, seizures, or loss of consciousness requiring immediate parenteral intervention..

Drug or chemical induced diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus With Hyperglycemia: [LLM DRAFT] Characterized by autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells, typically presenting with absolute insulin deficiency and ketosis-proneness. Compared to Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus With Hyperglycemia: [LLM DRAFT] Driven by peripheral insulin resistance and progressive secretory defect, often associated with metabolic syndrome features rather than recent exposure to a diabetogenic medication. Compared to Diabetes Mellitus Due To Underlying Condition With Hyperglycemia: [LLM DRAFT] Hyperglycemia directly caused by a distinct underlying systemic or endocrinological pathology (such as Cushing's syndrome or pancreatitis) rather than exogenous chemicals or drugs.

Dyshormogenetic goiter: A goiter caused by impaired synthesis or action of thyroid hormones, leading to compensatory thyroid enlargement. Common presenting complaints: Thyroid Swelling. Associated symptoms: none listed. Risk factors: none listed. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Dyshormogenetic goiter red flags. Red flag (RF_THYROTOXIC_CRISIS) triggered by complaint 'THYROTOXICOSIS': [LLM DRAFT] Severe thyrotoxicosis or thyroid storm presenting with fever, altered mental status, and hemodynamic instability in the context of dyshormogenetic goiter..

Dyshormogenetic goiter differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Congenital Hypothyroidism With Diffuse Goiter: [LLM DRAFT] Presents at birth with a diffuse thyroid enlargement due to inherited enzymatic defects in thyroid hormone synthesis, similar to dyshormogenetic goiter but typically recognized earlier via newborn screening. Compared to Nontoxic Diffuse Goiter: [LLM DRAFT] Represents an enlargement of the thyroid gland due to iodine deficiency or other non-genetic factors rather than an intrinsic inborn error of thyroid hormoneogenesis. Compared to Hypothyroidism Due To Medicaments And Other Exogenous Substances: [LLM DRAFT] Caused by exogenous goitrogens, drugs, or environmental agents inhibiting thyroid function rather than an inherited genetic defect in hormone synthesis.

Hypercalcemia of malignancy: Hypercalcemia of malignancy is an elevated serum calcium level caused by tumor-related secretion of parathyroid hormone-related peptide or osteolytic bone metastases. Common presenting complaints: Hypercalcemia. Associated symptoms: none listed. Risk factors: none listed. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Hypercalcemia of malignancy red flags. Red flag (RF_ALTERED_MENTAL_STATUS) triggered by complaint 'HYPERCALCEMIA': [LLM DRAFT] Serum Ca > 14 mg/dL with confusion, seizures, or coma. Red flag (RF_CARDIAC_ARRHYTHMIA) triggered by complaint 'HYPERCALCEMIA': [LLM DRAFT] Serum Ca > 14 mg/dL with arrhythmia or syncope.

Hypertrophy of breast: Breast hypertrophy is a rare medical condition of the breast connective tissues in which the breasts become excessively large. The condition is often divided based on the severity into two types, macromastia and gigantomastia. Common presenting complaints: Gynecomastia. Associated symptoms: Excessively Large Breast Tissue. Risk factors: none listed. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Hypertrophy of breast differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus With Hyperglycemia: [LLM DRAFT] Presents with polyuria, polydipsia, and weight loss rather than localized breast enlargement. Compared to Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus With Hyperglycemia: [LLM DRAFT] Associated with insulin resistance and metabolic syndrome features rather than primary breast tissue growth. Compared to Nontoxic Diffuse Goiter: [LLM DRAFT] Involves anterior neck swelling (thyroid enlargement) rather than breast tissue hypertrophy.

Hypoglycemia level 1: Hypoglycemia level 1 is a mild drop in blood glucose below normal thresholds, often asymptomatic or presenting with mild adrenergic symptoms. Common presenting complaints: Hypoglycemia. Associated symptoms: Clumsiness, Difficulty Talking, Confusion, Loss Of Consciousness, And Other Symptoms Related To Hypoglycemia. Risk factors: Gastric Bypass Surgery, Over Secretion Of Insulin. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Hypoglycemia level 1 differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Hypoglycemia Level 2: [LLM DRAFT] Defined by a lower blood glucose threshold (typically <54 mg/dL) indicating more severe neuroglycopenic risk than level 1. Compared to Hypoglycemia Level 3: [LLM DRAFT] Defined by severe cognitive impairment requiring external assistance for recovery, unlike the self-treatable level 1. Compared to Drug Induced Hypoglycemia Without Coma: [LLM DRAFT] Caused specifically by exogenous medications or chemicals rather than endogenous metabolic dysregulation, without progressing to coma.

Hypoglycemia level 2: A moderate drop in blood glucose requiring intervention but not life-threatening. Common presenting complaints: Hypoglycemia. Associated symptoms: Clumsiness, Difficulty Talking, Confusion, Loss Of Consciousness, And Other Symptoms Related To Hypoglycemia. Risk factors: Gastric Bypass Surgery, Over Secretion Of Insulin. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Hypoglycemia level 2 red flags. Red flag (RF_SEVERE_HYPOGLYCEMIA) triggered by complaint 'HYPOGLYCEMIA': [LLM DRAFT] When blood glucose drops to level 2 (<54 mg/dL) and is accompanied by severe cognitive impairment, altered mental status, or inability to safely consume oral carbohydrates, requiring assistance from another person..

Hypoglycemia level 2 differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Hypoglycemia Level 1: [LLM DRAFT] Defined by a higher blood glucose threshold (70 mg/dL to <54 mg/dL) with milder or absent neuroglycopenic symptoms compared to Level 2 (<54 mg/dL). Compared to Hypoglycemia Level 3: [LLM DRAFT] Defined as a severe clinical event characterized by altered mental and/or physical status requiring assistance, regardless of a specific blood glucose threshold. Compared to Drug Induced Hypoglycemia Without Coma: [LLM DRAFT] Identified by a clear temporal association with exogenous glucose-lowering medications or substances in a non-comatose patient.

Hypoglycemia level 3: A severe hypoglycemic episode with neuroglycopenic symptoms requiring immediate medical intervention. Common presenting complaints: Hypoglycemia. Associated symptoms: Clumsiness, Difficulty Talking, Confusion, Loss Of Consciousness, And Other Symptoms Related To Hypoglycemia. Risk factors: Gastric Bypass Surgery, Over Secretion Of Insulin. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Hypoglycemia level 3 red flags. Red flag (RF_HYPOGLYCEMIA_LEVEL_3) triggered by complaint 'HYPOGLYCEMIA': [LLM DRAFT] Severe level 3 hypoglycemia characterized by altered mental status, unresponsiveness, or inability to safely consume oral carbohydrates requiring parenteral rescue therapy..

Hypoglycemia level 3 differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Hypoglycemia Level 1: [LLM DRAFT] Milder blood glucose reduction characterized by self-treatable neuroglycopenic symptoms without severe cognitive impairment Compared to Hypoglycemia Level 2: [LLM DRAFT] Clinically significant hypoglycemia defined by a glucose threshold below 54 mg/dL requiring prompt action but lacking the severe altered mental status of Level 3 Compared to Drug Induced Hypoglycemia Without Coma: [LLM DRAFT] Hypoglycemia precipitated by exogenous medications or substances where full preservation of consciousness distinguishes it from severe level 3 episodes involving coma or profound impairment

Hypoglycemia, unspecified: Hypoglycemia, also spelled hypoglycaemia or hypoglycæmia, sometimes called low blood sugar, is a fall in blood sugar to levels below normal, typically below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L). Whipple's triad is used to properly identify hypoglycemic episodes. Common presenting complaints: Hypoglycemia. Associated symptoms: Headache, Blurred Vision, Shakiness, Dizziness, Weakness, Fatigue, Sweating, Clamminess, Fast Heart Rate, Anxiety, Hunger, Nausea. Risk factors: Medications (insulin, Glinides, And Sulfonylureas), Sepsis, Kidney Failure, Certain Tumors, Liver Disease. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Hypoglycemia, unspecified red flags. Red flag (RF_RED_FLAG_NAME) triggered by complaint 'HYPOGLYCEMIA': [LLM DRAFT] Severe hypoglycemia resulting in altered mental status, confusion, seizures, or loss of consciousness requiring immediate parenteral glucose or glucagon..

Hypoglycemia, unspecified differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Drug Induced Hypoglycemia Without Coma: [LLM DRAFT] History of recent administration of glucose-lowering medications or exogenous chemicals Compared to Iatrogenic Neonatal Hypoglycemia: [LLM DRAFT] History of clinical interventions or maternal factors immediately following birth in a newborn Compared to Hypoglycemia Level 3: [LLM DRAFT] Presence of severe cognitive impairment or physical assistance required from another person due to neuroglycopenia

Hypothyroidism due to medicaments and other exogenous substances: Hypothyroidism is an endocrine disease in which the thyroid gland does not produce enough thyroid hormones. It can cause a number of symptoms, such as poor ability to tolerate cold, extreme fatigue, muscle aches, constipation, slow heart rate, depression, and weight gain. Common presenting complaints: Hypothyroidism. Associated symptoms: Fatigue, Poor Ability To Tolerate Cold, Muscle Aches, Constipation, Weight Gain. Risk factors: Hashimotos Thyroiditis, Thyroiditis, Surgical Removal Of Thyroid Gland, Iodine Deficiency, Lithium Treatment. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Hypothyroidism due to medicaments and other exogenous substances red flags. Red flag (RF_HYPOTHEMIA_AND_MYXEDEMA_COMA) triggered by complaint 'HYPOTHYROIDISM': [LLM DRAFT] Severe drug-induced hypothyroidism progressing to altered mental status, hypothermia, and myxedema coma requiring immediate resuscitation..

Hypothyroidism due to medicaments and other exogenous substances differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Hypothyroidism Unspecified: [LLM DRAFT] Absence of a clearly identifiable history of causative medication or exogenous substance exposure Compared to Postprocedural Hypothyroidism: [LLM DRAFT] History of prior thyroid surgery, radioactive iodine therapy, or external neck radiation rather than exogenous agents Compared to Chronic Thyroiditis With Transient Thyrotoxicosis: [LLM DRAFT] Presence of autoimmune markers and an initial phase of excess thyroid hormone rather than isolated drug-induced underactivity

Hypothyroidism, unspecified: Hypothyroidism is an endocrine disease in which the thyroid gland does not produce enough thyroid hormones. It can cause a number of symptoms, such as poor ability to tolerate cold, extreme fatigue, muscle aches, constipation, slow heart rate, depression, and weight gain. Common presenting complaints: Hypothyroidism. Associated symptoms: Fatigue, Poor Ability To Tolerate Cold, Muscle Aches, Constipation, Weight Gain. Risk factors: Hashimotos Thyroiditis, Thyroiditis, Surgical Removal Of Thyroid Gland, Iodine Deficiency, Lithium Treatment. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Hypothyroidism, unspecified red flags. Red flag (RF_HYPOTROPIC_COMA) triggered by complaint 'HYPOTHYROIDISM': [LLM DRAFT] Severe myxedema coma characterized by hypothermia, altered mental status, hypoventilation, and hemodynamic instability in the setting of untreated or poorly managed hypothyroidism..

Hypothyroidism, unspecified differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Hypothyroidism Due To Medicaments And Other Exogenous Substances: [LLM DRAFT] History of exposure to offending drugs or exogenous substances known to impair thyroid function. Compared to Postprocedural Hypothyroidism: [LLM DRAFT] History of prior thyroid surgery, neck irradiation, or radioiodine ablation. Compared to Chronic Thyroiditis With Transient Thyrotoxicosis: [LLM DRAFT] Initial phase presenting with hyperthyroidism symptoms and elevated thyroid hormones before progressing to hypothyroidism.

Iatrogenic neonatal hypoglycemia: Iatrogenic neonatal hypoglycemia is a transient low blood glucose condition in newborns caused by medical interventions such as excessive glucose infusion or delayed feeding. Common presenting complaints: Hypoglycemia. Associated symptoms: Headache, Blurred Vision, Shakiness, Dizziness, Weakness, Fatigue, Sweating, Clamminess, Fast Heart Rate, Anxiety, Hunger, Nausea. Risk factors: Medications (insulin, Glinides, And Sulfonylureas), Sepsis, Kidney Failure, Certain Tumors, Liver Disease. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Iatrogenic neonatal hypoglycemia red flags. Red flag (RF_HYPOGLYCEMIA_CRISIS) triggered by complaint 'HYPOGLYCEMIA': [LLM DRAFT] Severe symptomatic iatrogenic neonatal hypoglycemia presenting with seizures, apnea, cyanosis, or lethargy unresponsive to feeding..

Iatrogenic neonatal hypoglycemia differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Other Neonatal Hypoglycemia: [LLM DRAFT] Presents with low blood glucose due to intrinsic factors (e.g., prematurity, intrauterine growth restriction) rather than exogenous medical intervention. Compared to Drug Induced Hypoglycemia Without Coma: [LLM DRAFT] Occurs in older children or adults rather than the neonatal period, typically related to medications like insulin or sulfonylureas. Compared to Hypoglycemia Unspecified: [LLM DRAFT] General diagnostic category used when the exact etiology (such as iatrogenic causes or specific metabolic disorders) has not yet been determined.

Neonatal goiter, not elsewhere classified: A thyroid enlargement in a newborn due to iodine deficiency or maternal thyroid disease, presenting with neck swelling and potential compressive symptoms. Common presenting complaints: Thyroid Swelling. Associated symptoms: none listed. Risk factors: Iodine Deficiency, Autoimmune Disease, Tumors, Cyanide Poisoning. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Neonatal goiter, not elsewhere classified red flags. Red flag (RF_THYROID_SWELLING_RESPIRATORY_DISTRESS) triggered by complaint 'THYROID_SWELLING': [LLM DRAFT] Severe neonatal goiter causing tracheal compression, airway obstruction, stridor, or acute respiratory distress requiring immediate airway management.. Red flag (RF_NEONATAL_THYROTOXIC_CRISIS) triggered by complaint 'THYROTOXICOSIS': [LLM DRAFT] Neonatal thyrotoxicosis presenting with severe tachycardia, heart failure, pyrexia, and irritability due to transplacental TSH receptor antibodies..

Neonatal goiter, not elsewhere classified differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Congenital Hypothyroidism With Diffuse Goiter: [LLM DRAFT] Associated with impaired thyroid hormone synthesis (dyshormonogenesis) leading to elevated TSH and gland enlargement present at birth. Compared to Dyshormogenetic Goiter: [LLM DRAFT] Caused by an intrinsic enzymatic defect in thyroid hormone biosynthesis rather than maternal or exogenous factors. Compared to Hypothyroidism Due To Medicaments And Other Exogenous Substances: [LLM DRAFT] History of maternal exposure to goitrogens (such as antithyroid drugs, iodides, or lithium) crossing the placenta.

Nontoxic diffuse goiter: Diffuse enlargement of the thyroid gland without evidence of hyperthyroidism, often due to iodine deficiency or other non-toxic causes. Common presenting complaints: Thyroid Swelling. Associated symptoms: Weight Gain, Feeling Tired, Constipation, Joint And Muscle Pain, Cold Intolerance, Dry Skin, Hair Loss, Slowed Heart Rate. Risk factors: Genetic And Environmental Factors. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Nontoxic diffuse goiter red flags. Red flag (RF_THYROTOXIC_CRISIS) triggered by complaint 'THYROTOXICOSIS': [LLM DRAFT] Acute, life-threatening exacerbation of thyrotoxicosis featuring severe hyperthermia, tachycardia, and altered mental status.. Red flag (RF_ACUTE_AIRWAY_COMPROMISE) triggered by complaint 'THYROID_SWELLING': [LLM DRAFT] Severe, rapidly progressive thyroid enlargement causing acute respiratory distress, stridor, or upper airway obstruction..

Nontoxic diffuse goiter differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Nontoxic Multinodular Goiter: [LLM DRAFT] Thyroid gland is multinodular on palpation or imaging rather than diffusely enlarged and smooth Compared to Dyshormogenetic Goiter: [LLM DRAFT] Typically presents in neonates or children with an inherited defect in thyroid hormone synthesis Compared to Chronic Thyroiditis With Transient Thyrotoxicosis: [LLM DRAFT] Presents with initial features of thyrotoxicosis and often elevated thyroid autoantibodies

Nontoxic goiter, unspecified: A diffuse enlargement of the thyroid gland without associated hyperthyroidism or hypothyroidism. Common presenting complaints: Thyroid Swelling. Associated symptoms: Neck Swelling, Compressive Symptoms Of Neck (difficulty Breathing, Difficulty Swallowing, Voice Changes). Risk factors: Iodine Deficiency Most Common. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Nontoxic goiter, unspecified red flags. Red flag (RF_ACUTE_AIRWAY_OBSTRUCTION_DUE_TO_RAPID_GOITER_EXPANSION) triggered by complaint 'THYROID_SWELLING': [LLM DRAFT] Rapid enlargement of a nontoxic goiter causing severe respiratory distress, stridor, or tracheal compression.. Red flag (RF_THYROTOXIC_STORM_INDUCED_BY_MULTINODULAR_GOITER) triggered by complaint 'THYROTOXICOSIS': [LLM DRAFT] Acute, life-threatening exacerbation of thyrotoxicosis featuring high fever, tachyarrhythmias, and altered mental status..

Nontoxic goiter, unspecified differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Nontoxic Diffuse Goiter: [LLM DRAFT] Presents with a smooth, symmetrical thyroid enlargement rather than an unspecified structural pattern. Compared to Nontoxic Multinodular Goiter: [LLM DRAFT] Characterized by multiple distinct nodules palpated throughout the thyroid gland. Compared to Dyshormogenetic Goiter: [LLM DRAFT] Caused by an inherited defect in thyroid hormone synthesis, frequently presenting early in life with associated hypothyroidism.

Nontoxic multinodular goiter: Nontoxic multinodular goitre, also known as an inactive multinodular goitre, is an enlargement of the thyroid gland, which develops multiple nodules without affecting thyroid hormone function. In the United States it is the most common cause of an enlarged thyroid, affecting between 3–5% of the population. Common presenting complaints: Thyroid Swelling. Associated symptoms: Neck Swelling, Compressive Symptoms Of Neck (difficulty Breathing, Difficulty Swallowing, Voice Changes). Risk factors: Iodine Deficiency Most Common. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Nontoxic multinodular goiter red flags. Red flag (RF_THYROID_SWELLING) triggered by complaint 'THYROID_SWELLING': [LLM DRAFT] Acute, rapid enlargement of a multinodular goiter causing severe compression of the trachea or esophagus, presenting with acute respiratory distress, stridor, or severe dysphagia.. Red flag (RF_THYROTOXICOSIS) triggered by complaint 'THYROTOXICOSIS': [LLM DRAFT] Acute manifestation of thyrotoxicosis (thyroid storm) associated with a multinodular goiter, presenting with hyperpyrexia, tachycardia, altered mental status, and gastrointestinal dysfunction..

Nontoxic multinodular goiter differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Nontoxic Diffuse Goiter: [LLM DRAFT] Presents with a smooth, symmetrical thyroid enlargement rather than multiple distinct palpable nodules. Compared to Chronic Thyroiditis With Transient Thyrotoxicosis: [LLM DRAFT] Features transient biochemical thyrotoxicosis and inflammatory markers or thyroid autoantibodies rather than normal thyroid function and multinodularity. Compared to Other Specified Nontoxic Goiter: [LLM DRAFT] Involves specific etiology or structural characteristics not classified under standard multinodular goiter.

Other hypoglycemia: Hypoglycemia, also spelled hypoglycaemia or hypoglycæmia, sometimes called low blood sugar, is a fall in blood sugar to levels below normal, typically below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L). Whipple's triad is used to properly identify hypoglycemic episodes. Common presenting complaints: Hypoglycemia. Associated symptoms: Headache, Blurred Vision, Shakiness, Dizziness, Weakness, Fatigue, Sweating, Clamminess, Fast Heart Rate, Anxiety, Hunger, Nausea. Other hypoglycemia red flags. Red flag (RF_SEVERE_HYPOGLYCEMIA) triggered by complaint 'HYPOGLYCEMIA': [LLM DRAFT] Severe hypoglycemia presenting with altered mental status, unresponsiveness, or inability to safely consume oral glucose..

Other hypoglycemia differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Hypoglycemia Unspecified: [LLM DRAFT] Lack of specific etiology or classification details compared to other defined forms of hypoglycemia. Compared to Drug Induced Hypoglycemia Without Coma: [LLM DRAFT] Clear temporal association with the administration of insulin, oral hypoglycemic agents, or other causative medications without altered mental status. Compared to Other Neonatal Hypoglycemia: [LLM DRAFT] Presentation restricted strictly to the neonatal period, typically linked to perinatal stressors, prematurity, or maternal factors.

Other neonatal hypocalcemia: Neonatal hypocalcemia is an abnormal clinical and laboratory hypocalcemia condition that is frequently observed in infants. It is commonly presented within the first 72 hours of a newborn's life. Common presenting complaints: Hypocalcemia. Associated symptoms: none listed. Risk factors: none listed. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Other neonatal hypocalcemia differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Cows Milk Hypocalcemia In Newborn: [LLM DRAFT] History of high-phosphate cow's milk formula ingestion leading to secondary hypocalcemia Compared to Autosomal Dominant Hypocalcemia: [LLM DRAFT] Activating mutations in the calcium-sensing receptor causing autosomal dominant inheritance and hypocalcemia with inappropriately normal or low PTH Compared to Congenital Hypothyroidism Without Goiter: [LLM DRAFT] Presents with prolonged jaundice, feeding difficulties, and hypotonia rather than primary neuromuscular irritability from hypocalcemia

Other neonatal hypoglycemia: Neonatal hypoglycemia, or low blood sugar in newborn babies, occurs when an infant's blood glucose level is below normal. Diagnostic thresholds vary internationally. Common presenting complaints: Hypoglycemia. Associated symptoms: none listed. Risk factors: Hyperinsulinism, Limited Glycogen Stores, Increases Glucose Use, Decreased Gluconeogenesis, Depleted Glycogen Stores. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Other neonatal hypoglycemia red flags. Red flag (RF_HYPOGLYCEMIA) triggered by complaint 'HYPOGLYCEMIA': [LLM DRAFT] Severe symptomatic neonatal hypoglycemia presenting with lethargy, apnea, seizures, or poor feeding unresponsive to initial feeding..

Other neonatal hypoglycemia differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Iatrogenic Neonatal Hypoglycemia: [LLM DRAFT] History of exogenous insulin administration or glucose-lowering medical intervention in the neonate. Compared to Hypoglycemia Unspecified: [LLM DRAFT] Applies when specific etiology or neonatal status details are not documented or known. Compared to Other Hypoglycemia: [LLM DRAFT] Occurs in non-neonates or broader clinical contexts outside the newborn period.

Other specified diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia: Diabetes mellitus, commonly known as diabetes, is a group of common endocrine diseases characterized by sustained high blood sugar levels. Diabetes tends to progress in severity, and is due to either a reduced production of the hormone insulin by the pancreas or unresponsiveness of bodily cells to insulin's effects. Common presenting complaints: Hyperglycemia. Associated symptoms: Frequent Urination, Increased Thirst, Increased Hunger. Risk factors: Insulin Insufficiency Or Gradual Resistance. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Other specified diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia red flags. Red flag (RF_HYPERGLYCEMIA) triggered by complaint 'HYPERGLYCEMIA': [LLM DRAFT] Severe hyperglycemia accompanied by altered mental status, confusion, lethargy, or signs of diabetic ketoacidosis (such as Kussmaul breathing or fruity breath).. Red flag (RF_HYPOGLYCEMIA) triggered by complaint 'HYPOGLYCEMIA': [LLM DRAFT] Severe hypoglycemia presenting with loss of consciousness, seizures, or inability to safely ingest oral glucose..

Other specified diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus With Hyperglycemia: [LLM DRAFT] Presents with absolute insulin deficiency, often requiring lifelong insulin therapy from onset. Compared to Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus With Hyperglycemia: [LLM DRAFT] Characterized predominantly by insulin resistance and relative insulin deficiency, typically associated with metabolic syndrome. Compared to Drug Or Chemical Induced Diabetes Mellitus With Hyperglycemia: [LLM DRAFT] Onset directly correlates with the initiation of a specific causative medication or chemical exposure.

Other specified hypothyroidism: Hypothyroidism is an endocrine disease in which the thyroid gland does not produce enough thyroid hormones. It can cause a number of symptoms, such as poor ability to tolerate cold, extreme fatigue, muscle aches, constipation, slow heart rate, depression, and weight gain. Common presenting complaints: Hypothyroidism. Associated symptoms: none listed. Risk factors: none listed. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Other specified hypothyroidism red flags. Red flag (RF_MYXEDEMA_COMA) triggered by complaint 'HYPOTHYROIDISM': [LLM DRAFT] Severe altered mental status, hypothermia, hypoventilation, and hypotension indicative of decompensated hypothyroidism..

Other specified hypothyroidism differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Hypothyroidism Due To Medicaments And Other Exogenous Substances: [LLM DRAFT] History of exposure to goitrogens, lithium, amiodarone, or antithyroid medications rather than intrinsic primary thyroid pathology. Compared to Postprocedural Hypothyroidism: [LLM DRAFT] History of prior thyroidectomy, radioactive iodine ablation, or external neck radiation therapy. Compared to Congenital Hypothyroidism Without Goiter: [LLM DRAFT] Presents in the neonatal period with thyroid dysgenesis or absence rather than acquired specific etiologies in older individuals.

Other specified nontoxic goiter: A slowly enlarging thyroid gland without evidence of hyperthyroidism or iodine deficiency, often diagnosed after other causes are excluded. Common presenting complaints: Thyroid Swelling. Associated symptoms: none listed. Risk factors: none listed. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Other specified nontoxic goiter red flags. Red flag (RF_THYROID_SWELLING) triggered by complaint 'THYROID_SWELLING': [LLM DRAFT] Acute, rapidly enlarging nontoxic goiter causing severe respiratory distress, stridor, or tracheal compression.. Red flag (RF_THYROTOXICOSIS) triggered by complaint 'THYROTOXICOSIS': [LLM DRAFT] Precipitation of severe thyrotoxic crisis (thyroid storm) with hyperthermia, tachycardia, and altered mental status..

Other specified nontoxic goiter differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Nontoxic Diffuse Goiter: [LLM DRAFT] Uniform thyroid enlargement without discrete nodularity or specific underlying metabolic defects. Compared to Nontoxic Multinodular Goiter: [LLM DRAFT] Presence of multiple distinct nodules throughout an enlarged thyroid gland rather than a single or other atypical presentation. Compared to Dyshormogenetic Goiter: [LLM DRAFT] Caused by an intrinsic inborn error of thyroid hormone synthesis rather than other specified exogenous or rare nontoxic factors.

Other thyrotoxicosis with thyrotoxic crisis or storm: Hyperthyroidism is a endocrine disease in which the thyroid gland produces excessive amounts of thyroid hormones. Thyrotoxicosis is a condition that occurs due to elevated levels of thyroid hormones of any cause and therefore includes hyperthyroidism. Common presenting complaints: Thyrotoxicosis. Associated symptoms: Irritability, Muscle Weakness, Sleeping Problems, Fast Heartbeat, Heat Intolerance, Diarrhea, Enlargement Of The Thyroid, Weight Loss. Risk factors: Graves Disease, Multinodular Goiter, Toxic Adenoma, Inflammation Of The Thyroid, Eating Too Much Iodine, Too Much Synthetic Thyroid Hormone. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Other thyrotoxicosis with thyrotoxic crisis or storm red flags. Red flag (RF_THYROTOXICOSIS) triggered by complaint 'THYROTOXICOSIS': [LLM DRAFT] Thyrotoxic storm with acute altered mental status, high fever, and hemodynamic instability requiring immediate life-saving intervention..

Other thyrotoxicosis with thyrotoxic crisis or storm differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Thyrotoxicosis Factitia With Thyrotoxic Crisis Or Storm: [LLM DRAFT] History of exogenous thyroid hormone ingestion with low radioactive iodine uptake Compared to Thyrotoxicosis Unspecified With Thyrotoxic Crisis Or Storm: [LLM DRAFT] Severe hypermetabolic state with multiorgan failure where the specific underlying etiology is yet undetermined Compared to Chronic Thyroiditis With Transient Thyrotoxicosis: [LLM DRAFT] Initial hyperthyroid phase due to follicular leakage followed by eventual hypothyroidism, typically lacking severe storm features

Other thyrotoxicosis without thyrotoxic crisis or storm: Hyperthyroidism is a endocrine disease in which the thyroid gland produces excessive amounts of thyroid hormones. Thyrotoxicosis is a condition that occurs due to elevated levels of thyroid hormones of any cause and therefore includes hyperthyroidism. Common presenting complaints: Thyrotoxicosis. Associated symptoms: Irritability, Muscle Weakness, Sleeping Problems, Fast Heartbeat, Heat Intolerance, Diarrhea, Enlargement Of The Thyroid, Weight Loss. Risk factors: Graves Disease, Multinodular Goiter, Toxic Adenoma, Inflammation Of The Thyroid, Eating Too Much Iodine, Too Much Synthetic Thyroid Hormone. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Other thyrotoxicosis without thyrotoxic crisis or storm differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Chronic Thyroiditis With Transient Thyrotoxicosis: [LLM DRAFT] Presents with initial painful or painless thyroiditis and transient hormone release followed by eventual hypothyroidism. Compared to Thyrotoxicosis Factitia Without Thyrotoxic Crisis Or Storm: [LLM DRAFT] Caused by exogenous thyroid hormone ingestion, characterized by a low radioactive iodine uptake and low serum thyroglobulin levels. Compared to Thyrotoxicosis With Diffuse Goiter Without Thyrotoxic Crisis Or Storm: [LLM DRAFT] Classic Graves' disease presentation featuring autoimmune diffuse goiter, ophthalmopathy, and/or dermopathy.

Postinfectious hypothyroidism: Postinfectious hypothyroidism is a delayed onset of hypothyroid symptoms following an acute viral or bacterial infection. Common presenting complaints: Hypothyroidism. Associated symptoms: Diarrhea, Constipation, Abdominal Pain, Flatulence, Frequent Urination. Risk factors: Unknown. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Postinfectious hypothyroidism red flags. Red flag (RF_HYPOTHYROIDISM) triggered by complaint 'HYPOTHYROIDISM': [LLM DRAFT] Severe myxedema coma characterized by hypothermia, altered mental status, and hypoventilation following a postinfectious thyroiditis event..

Postinfectious hypothyroidism differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Chronic Thyroiditis With Transient Thyrotoxicosis: [LLM DRAFT] Presents with an initial phase of excess thyroid hormone release before eventual normalization or hypothyroidism. Compared to Hypothyroidism Due To Medicaments And Other Exogenous Substances: [LLM DRAFT] History of exposure to specific drugs or exogenous agents known to impair thyroid function. Compared to Postprocedural Hypothyroidism: [LLM DRAFT] History of surgical thyroidectomy, radioactive iodine ablation, or external neck radiation therapy.

Postprocedural hypothyroidism: Postprocedural hypothyroidism is a transient or permanent reduction in thyroid hormone production following thyroid surgery, radioiodine therapy, or neck irradiation. Common presenting complaints: Hypothyroidism. Associated symptoms: none listed. Risk factors: none listed. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Postprocedural hypothyroidism red flags. Red flag (RF_HYPOCALCEMIA) triggered by complaint 'HYPOCALCEMIA': [LLM DRAFT] Severe postprocedural hypocalcemia presenting with carpopedal spasm, tetany, or QT prolongation following total thyroidectomy.. Red flag (RF_THYROTOXICOSIS) triggered by complaint 'THYROTOXICOSIS': [LLM DRAFT] Postprocedural thyroid storm presenting with high fever, tachycardia, and altered mental status due to manipulation of the thyroid gland during surgery..

Postprocedural hypothyroidism differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Hypothyroidism Due To Medicaments And Other Exogenous Substances: [LLM DRAFT] History of inciting drug or exogenous substance exposure rather than surgical or procedural intervention Compared to Hypothyroidism Unspecified: [LLM DRAFT] Absence of a documented history of thyroid surgery, neck irradiation, or medical procedures involving the thyroid Compared to Postinfectious Hypothyroidism: [LLM DRAFT] Preceding history of an infectious or inflammatory thyroid illness rather than an iatrogenic procedure

Primary hyperparathyroidism: Primary hyperparathyroidism is a medical condition where the parathyroid gland produce excess amounts of parathyroid hormone (PTH). The symptoms of the condition relate to the resulting elevated serum calcium (hypercalcemia), which can cause digestive symptoms, kidney stones, psychiatric abnormalities, and bone disease. Common presenting complaints: Hypercalcemia. Associated symptoms: none listed. Risk factors: none listed. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Primary hyperparathyroidism red flags. Red flag (RF_HYPERCALCEMIC_CRISIS) triggered by complaint 'HYPERCALCEMIA': [LLM DRAFT] Severe hypercalcemia (typically calcium > 14 mg/dL or with acute encephalopathy/cardiac instability) secondary to primary hyperparathyroidism requiring immediate life-saving medical intervention..

Subclinical iodine-deficiency hypothyroidism: A mild form of hypothyroidism caused by insufficient iodine intake, presenting with subtle biochemical changes but minimal clinical symptoms. Common presenting complaints: Hypothyroidism. Associated symptoms: Fatigue, Poor Ability To Tolerate Cold, Muscle Aches, Constipation, Weight Gain. Risk factors: Hashimotos Thyroiditis, Thyroiditis, Surgical Removal Of Thyroid Gland, Iodine Deficiency, Lithium Treatment. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Subclinical iodine-deficiency hypothyroidism differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Hypothyroidism Unspecified: [LLM DRAFT] Normal free T4 with a mildly elevated TSH can confirm subclinical disease versus overt hypothyroidism where free T4 is low. Compared to Chronic Thyroiditis With Transient Thyrotoxicosis: [LLM DRAFT] Presents with initial hyperthyroidism symptoms and suppressed TSH rather than mildly elevated TSH typical of subclinical hypothyroidism. Compared to Nontoxic Diffuse Goiter: [LLM DRAFT] Features normal thyroid function tests (normal TSH and free T4) in contrast to the elevated TSH seen in subclinical hypothyroidism.

Thyrotoxicosis factitia with thyrotoxic crisis or storm: Thyrotoxicosis factitia is a condition of thyrotoxicosis caused by the ingestion of exogenous thyroid hormone. It can be the result of mistaken ingestion of excess drugs, such as levothyroxine and triiodothyronine, or as a symptom of Munchausen syndrome. Common presenting complaints: Thyrotoxicosis. Associated symptoms: none listed. Risk factors: none listed. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Thyrotoxicosis factitia with thyrotoxic crisis or storm red flags. Red flag (RF_THYROTOXIC_STORM) triggered by complaint 'THYROTOXICOSIS': [LLM DRAFT] Presentation with signs of thyroid storm including severe hyperthermia, tachycardia out of proportion to fever, altered mental status, and gastrointestinal dysfunction in a patient with thyrotoxicosis factitia..

Thyrotoxicosis factitia with thyrotoxic crisis or storm differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Other Thyrotoxicosis With Thyrotoxic Crisis Or Storm: [LLM DRAFT] Presents with hyperthyroid storm symptoms due to endogenous overproduction rather than exogenous hormone ingestion. Compared to Thyrotoxicosis Factitia Without Thyrotoxic Crisis Or Storm: [LLM DRAFT] Presents with biochemical thyrotoxicosis from exogenous hormone use but lacks the life-threatening systemic decompensation of a storm. Compared to Thyrotoxicosis Unspecified With Thyrotoxic Crisis Or Storm: [LLM DRAFT] Features acute life-threatening storm symptoms where the specific endogenous or exogenous etiology has not yet been determined.

Thyrotoxicosis factitia without thyrotoxic crisis or storm: Thyrotoxicosis factitia is a condition of thyrotoxicosis caused by the ingestion of exogenous thyroid hormone. It can be the result of mistaken ingestion of excess drugs, such as levothyroxine and triiodothyronine, or as a symptom of Munchausen syndrome. Common presenting complaints: Thyrotoxicosis. Associated symptoms: none listed. Risk factors: none listed. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Thyrotoxicosis factitia without thyrotoxic crisis or storm differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Chronic Thyroiditis With Transient Thyrotoxicosis: [LLM DRAFT] Presence of painful or tender thyroid gland accompanied by elevated inflammatory markers (e.g., ESR) during the destructive phase. Compared to Thyrotoxicosis With Diffuse Goiter Without Thyrotoxic Crisis Or Storm: [LLM DRAFT] Presence of a diffuse goiter and signs of autoimmunity such as ophthalmopathy or positive TSH receptor antibodies (Graves' disease). Compared to Other Thyrotoxicosis Without Thyrotoxic Crisis Or Storm: [LLM DRAFT] Endogenous hormone overproduction indicated by elevated radioactive iodine uptake, unlike the near-zero uptake seen in factitia.

Risk factors: Graves Disease, Multinodular Goiter, Toxic Adenoma, Inflammation Of The Thyroid, Eating Too Much Iodine, Too Much Synthetic Thyroid Hormone. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Thyrotoxicosis, unspecified with thyrotoxic crisis or storm red flags. Red flag (RF_THYROTOXIC_STORM) triggered by complaint 'THYROTOXICOSIS': [LLM DRAFT] Severe thyrotoxic crisis characterized by high fever, marked tachycardia, altered mental status, and gastrointestinal dysfunction requiring immediate life-saving intervention..

Thyrotoxicosis, unspecified with thyrotoxic crisis or storm differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Other Thyrotoxicosis With Thyrotoxic Crisis Or Storm: [LLM DRAFT] Distinguished by a specific identified etiology (such as Graves' disease or toxic multinodular goiter) precipitating the storm, rather than an unspecified cause. Compared to Thyrotoxicosis Factitia With Thyrotoxic Crisis Or Storm: [LLM DRAFT] Characterized by exogenous thyroid hormone ingestion, typically presenting with a low radioiodine uptake and low serum thyroglobulin levels. Compared to Chronic Thyroiditis With Transient Thyrotoxicosis: [LLM DRAFT] Usually presents with a painful or painless thyroiditis phase leading to self-limited hormone release, rarely progressing to a true thyroid storm.

Thyrotoxicosis, unspecified without thyrotoxic crisis or storm: Hyperthyroidism is a endocrine disease in which the thyroid gland produces excessive amounts of thyroid hormones. Thyrotoxicosis is a condition that occurs due to elevated levels of thyroid hormones of any cause and therefore includes hyperthyroidism. Common presenting complaints: Thyrotoxicosis. Associated symptoms: Irritability, Muscle Weakness, Sleeping Problems, Fast Heartbeat, Heat Intolerance, Diarrhea, Enlargement Of The Thyroid, Weight Loss. Acute or chronic: .

Red flag (RF_THYROTOXICOSIS) triggered by complaint 'THYROTOXICOSIS': [LLM DRAFT] Acute progression to thyroid storm characterized by high fever, severe tachycardia, altered mental status, and gastrointestinal symptoms in a patient with thyrotoxicosis..

Thyrotoxicosis, unspecified without thyrotoxic crisis or storm differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Chronic Thyroiditis With Transient Thyrotoxicosis: [LLM DRAFT] Presents with initial hyperthyroidism followed by spontaneous hypothyroidism and is often associated with painful or painless thyroiditis rather than primary hypersecretion. Compared to Thyrotoxicosis Unspecified With Thyrotoxic Crisis Or Storm: [LLM DRAFT] Presents with life-threatening systemic decompensation, high fever, and severe multi-organ dysfunction rather than stable excess thyroid hormone. Compared to Thyrotoxicosis Factitia Without Thyrotoxic Crisis Or Storm: [LLM DRAFT] Caused by exogenous thyroid hormone ingestion, typically demonstrating a low radioiodine uptake and suppressed thyroglobulin levels.

Thyrotoxicosis with diffuse goiter without thyrotoxic crisis or storm: Hyperthyroidism is a endocrine disease in which the thyroid gland produces excessive amounts of thyroid hormones. Associated symptoms: Irritability, Muscle Weakness, Sleeping Problems, Fast Heartbeat, Heat Intolerance, Diarrhea, Enlargement Of The Thyroid, Weight Loss. Risk factors: Graves Disease, Multinodular Goiter, Toxic Adenoma, Inflammation Of The Thyroid, Eating Too Much Iodine, Too Much Synthetic Thyroid Hormone. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Thyrotoxicosis with diffuse goiter without thyrotoxic crisis or storm red flags. Red flag (RF_THYROTOXICOSIS) triggered by complaint 'THYROTOXICOSIS': [LLM DRAFT] Onset of high fever, altered mental status, marked tachycardia, or gastrointestinal symptoms indicating progression to thyroid storm..

Thyrotoxicosis with diffuse goiter without thyrotoxic crisis or storm differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Chronic Thyroiditis With Transient Thyrotoxicosis: [LLM DRAFT] Presents with painful or painless thyroiditis leading to temporary thyroid hormone release followed by resolution or hypothyroidism, often with low radioactive iodine uptake. Compared to Dyshormogenetic Goiter: [LLM DRAFT] Typically presents in neonates or children with congenital defects in thyroid hormone synthesis, usually resulting in hypothyroidism rather than thyrotoxicosis despite the diffuse goiter. Compared to Nontoxic Diffuse Goiter: [LLM DRAFT] Characterized by a diffusely enlarged thyroid gland in the setting of normal thyroid function (euthyroid) without any biochemical evidence of thyrotoxicosis.

Type 1 diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia: Type 1 diabetes (T1D), or type 1 diabetes mellitus, is an autoimmune disease that occurs when the body's immune system destroys beta cells in the pancreas that produce the hormone insulin. Insulin is used by the body to store and convert blood sugar into energy. Common presenting complaints: Hyperglycemia. Associated symptoms: Frequent Urination, Increased Thirst, Weight Loss. Risk factors: Body Does Not Produce Enough Insulin. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Type 1 diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia red flags. Red flag (RF_HYPERGLYCEMIA) triggered by complaint 'HYPERGLYCEMIA': [LLM DRAFT] Severe hyperglycemia with altered mental status, confusion, or signs of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) such as Kussmaul breathing and fruity breath odor..

Type 1 diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus With Hyperglycemia: [LLM DRAFT] Typically presents with insulin resistance and metabolic syndrome features rather than absolute autoimmune insulin deficiency. Compared to Diabetes Mellitus Due To Underlying Condition With Hyperglycemia: [LLM DRAFT] Associated with specific secondary etiologies such as endocrinopathies, exocrine pancreatic disease, or identifiable genetic syndromes. Compared to Drug Or Chemical Induced Diabetes Mellitus With Hyperglycemia: [LLM DRAFT] Onset directly correlates with the initiation of specific diabetogenic medications such as glucocorticoids or antipsychotics.

Type 2 diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia: Type 2 diabetes (T2D), formerly known as adult-onset diabetes, is a form of diabetes mellitus that is characterized by high blood sugar, insulin resistance, and relative lack of insulin. Common symptoms include increased thirst, frequent urination, fatigue and unexplained weight loss. Common presenting complaints: Hyperglycemia. Associated symptoms: Increased Thirst, Frequent Urination, Unexplained Weight Loss, Increased Hunger. Risk factors: Obesity, Smoking. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Type 2 diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia red flags. Red flag (RF_HYPERGLYCEMIC_HYPEROSMOLAR_STATE) triggered by complaint 'HYPERGLYCEMIA': [LLM DRAFT] Severe hyperglycemia with altered mental status, dehydration, or hyperosmolarity requiring immediate emergency resuscitation.. Red flag (RF_DIABETIC_KETOACIDOSIS) triggered by complaint 'HYPERGLYCEMIA': [LLM DRAFT] Hyperglycemia complicated by nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and acidosis requiring immediate emergency intervention..

Type 2 diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Diabetes Mellitus Due To Underlying Condition With Hyperglycemia: [LLM DRAFT] Identifiable secondary endocrinopathy or systemic illness precipitating the hyperglycemia. Compared to Drug Or Chemical Induced Diabetes Mellitus With Hyperglycemia: [LLM DRAFT] Clear temporal association with the initiation of a culprit medication known to impair glucose tolerance. Compared to Other Specified Diabetes Mellitus With Hyperglycemia: [LLM DRAFT] Presence of uncommon genetic defects or atypical pathophysiologic mechanisms not characteristic of standard type 2 diabetes.
